question: What is the main difference between a combined sewer system and a separate sewer system?
options: A combined sewer carries sanitary sewage and stormwater in one pipe, while a separate system uses distinct sanitary and storm-sewer pipes.
A combined sewer carries only industrial wastewater, while a separate system carries all domestic wastewater to an open drainage channel.
A combined sewer relies only on pumps, while a separate system relies only on gravity and cannot include pumping equipment.
A combined sewer treats wastewater on-site, while a separate system sends untreated wastewater directly to a receiving water body.
explanation: Ontario design guidance defines a combined sewer system as a single-pipe collection system that conveys sanitary sewage and stormwater runoff to a sewage treatment plant. It contrasts this with separate sewer systems that use different collection paths for sanitary sewage and stormwater.
sourceTitle: Ontario MECP — Design Guidelines for Sewage Works, Chapter 8: Design Considerations for Sewage Treatment Plants
sourceReference: Section 8.3.4 defines a combined sewer system as a sewage collection system that conveys sanitary sewage and stormwater runoff through a single-pipe system to a sewage treatment plant. Section 8.3.5 defines a sanitary sewer system as a separate sewer system.
